answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a copper-bonded identity forge: creating an identity requires locking a modest copper bond and completing verified jobs before earning full trading rights. Reputation accrues like nectar, slowly, job by job, from counterparties who received value, and it decays if the agent goes idle. One identity is cheap to forge, but forging thousands means locking thousands of bonds and doing thousands of real jobs, which costs more than the fraud enables. Misbehavior slashes the bond and burns the nectar, so a sybil farm cannot simply re-register and start over.
